[1] repair-manual.pdf p.5
Sentinel 1000 and 1000 Pro
The Sentinel 1000 (LS-1000) and Sentinel 1000 Pro (LS-1000P) share one body and one
service procedure; the Pro has the larger pack, four light panels instead of two, and the solar
top. They carry a 5-year warranty, so most Sentinels on the bench are red tags. The faults are
a pack that will not hold charge, a panel latch that will not hold a panel, and the charge port.
Tools: a T8 Torx driver, the plastic spudger, the pack tester, and the latch spring tool.
Battery pack
The Sentinel 1000 battery pack is part B-1000-21 and is held by four T8 Torx screws. The
Pro's pack is part B-1000P-21, same mounting. A pack tests bad if it holds less than 70% of
its rated capacity after a full charge on the pack tester, or if it is swollen at all.
1. Discharge the lantern to below 20% on low before opening it. The charge indicator
shows one bar.

The Sentinel 1000 is the lantern we sell to people who lose power often. Its two light panels pull
off the body and run on their own for up to 6 hours each, so one lantern lights the kitchen while a
panel goes to the bathroom and another to the stairs. The body is sealed to IP67 and floats. The
10,000 mAh battery charges over USB-C in about 7 hours and can run a phone from the USB-A port for
several days. The Sentinel line carries a 5-year warranty on the lantern and panels; the battery,
as on every rechargeable product, is covered for 1 year.

Compatible parts: USB-C cable C-15, replacement panel P-1000, carry bag BG-1000.

The Sentinel 1000 Pro doubles the battery and the panel count of the Sentinel 1000 and adds a
4-watt solar panel in the lid. In full sun the solar top adds about 2 hours of high-mode runtime
per day, which is not enough to run the lantern on sun alone but will keep it topped up between
outages. Four panels mean four rooms lit from one base. At 1.9 kg it is a lantern to carry to the
car, not up a trail. Same IP67 sealing and the same 5-year warranty as the Sentinel 1000.

Compatible parts: USB-C cable C-15, replacement panel P-1000, carry bag BG-1000P.

### Scenario 2: a Sentinel 1000 Pro that stopped charging

On Thursday, September 3, 2026, a customer calls about a Sentinel 1000 Pro bought on June 14,
2025, order LS-2025-002210. It no longer charges from the wall or the solar top. The lantern is
inside its 5-year warranty, but the battery pack is inside its own 1-year battery warranty only
until June 14, 2026, which has passed. The agent opens warranty claim WC-030517 anyway, because
the fault may be the charging circuit rather than the pack, and explains that the Repair Center
will decide within 5 business days. On September 8 Walt Brannigan's team finds a failed charge
controller, which is a manufacturing defect covered by the 5-year warranty, and repairs it at no
charge under repair ticket RT-20931. The lantern ships back on September 11. Had the fault been
the pack alone, the agent would have quoted a paid pack replacement instead.

[5] customer-service-playbook.md > Warranty claims
## Warranty claims

The standard warranty is 2 years from the purchase date and covers manufacturing defects. The
Sentinel 1000 and Sentinel 1000 Pro carry 5 years, the Heritage No. 7 carries 10 years,
rechargeable batteries and battery packs carry 1 year, and Second Light refurbished items carry
1 year. Mantles, globes, wicks, bulbs and fuel caps are consumables and are not covered. Drops,
water beyond the IP rating, unapproved fuel, modifications and commercial rental use are not
covered.

A customer starts a claim by emailing help@lanternsupply.example with the order number and
photos. Open a warranty claim in the Hearth admin; it issues a number in the form WC-xxxxxx, for
example WC-030517. The Repair Center decides within 5 business days whether to repair or replace,
and the choice is ours. For an approved claim, send the customer a prepaid label to the
Hagerstown Repair Center at no charge. A claim with no order number can be matched by email
address or by the serial number on the base of the lantern.

The warranty transfers with a gift but not with a resale. If a customer bought the item second
hand, explain this and offer a paid repair.
